chunks.l2:
[tal-a17-v01] Then I speak the procedure that bestows identity with Bhairava-nature, thus in five: mandala, pot, fire, disciple, and self.

[tal-a17-v10] Having invoked and worshipped maya-shakti with one's own mantra, one should satisfy it; the matrika syllable is used in invocation, and the malini syllable in worship.

[tal-a17-v02] Having taken unity of pervasion, one places the path and the student's course; the three impurities—karma, māyā, and anu—are placed on the arm, on the throat, and likewise.

[tal-a17-v03] And the teacher should cast into the crest by thread-knot union; its appearance as other than its own form is impurity; that knot is called impurity.

[tal-a17-v04] For the firmness of the reply 'iti,' an external knot is arranged; the arms are the seat of action; the Vishnu-maya self dwells in the throat.

[tal-a17-v05] Thus imagination, made from the downward-flowing flame-atomicity, produces manifoldness in the triad called nara, shakti, and shiva.

[tal-a17-v06] To speak, one should arrange a ninefold thread for knotting; fire, water, and food are threefold, each in three ways.

[tal-a17-v07] At the end of hearing, some from this entered the white, black, and red; then in fire, having satisfied all mantras, they became consciousness-space only.

[tal-a17-v08] In the common form of the principles, one should practice gradual purification; there, by union with one's own mantra, one should first invoke earth.

[tal-a17-v09] Having worshipped with flowers and the like, one should then propitiate with ghee, sesame, and the like the deity pervading each principle, and afterwards the presiding deity of the māyā principle.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-:C17 atha śrītantrāloke saptadaśamāhnikam atha bhairavatādātmyadāyinīṃ prakriyāṃ bruve / evaṃ maṇḍalakumbhāgniśiṣyasvātmasu pañcasu gṛhītvā vyāptimaikyena nyasyādhvānaṃ ca śiṣyagam / karmamāyāṇumalinatrayaṃ bāhau gale tathā śikhāyāṃ ca kṣipetsūtragranthiyogena daiśikaḥ / tasyātadrūpatābhānaṃ malo granthiḥ sa kīrtyate itipratītidārḍhyārthaṃ bahirgranthyupakalpanam / bāhū karmāspadaṃ viṣṇurmāyātmā galasaṃśritaḥ adhovahā śikhāṇutvaṃ tenetthaṃ kalpanā kṛtā / naraśaktiśivākhyasya trayasya bahubhedatām vaktuṃ tristriguṇaṃ sūtraṃ granthaye parikalpayet / tejojalānnatritayaṃ tredhā pratyekamapyadaḥ śrutyante ke@pyataḥ śuklakṛṣṇaraktaṃ prapedire / tato@gnau tarpitāśeṣamantre cidvyomamātrake sāmānyarūpe tattvānāṃ kramācchuddhiṃ samācaret / tatra svamantrayogena dharāmāvāhayetpurā iṣṭvā puṣpādibhiḥ sarpistilādyairatha tarpayet / tattattvavyāpikāṃ paścānmāyātattvādhidevatām māyāśaktiṃ svamantreṇāvāhyābhyarcya pratarpayet / āvāhane mātṛkārṇaṃ mālinyarṇaṃ ca pūjane

chunks.l2:
[tal-a17-v11] The teacher said, "May he do thus," from the two nourishings of own form: the tāra syllable, the phoneme, and the address-word "you," hence beyond.

[tal-a17-v12] The action-word joined with the highest one is also a lamp from here; to you a name ending in the fourth case; then also a suitable lamp.

[tal-a17-v13] By the mantra-yoga of reasoning one should perform the respective action; indeed after invocation all action is declared.

[tal-a17-v14] Invocation and awakening are the establishment of one's own nature; there is absorption into one's own self-identity.

[tal-a17-v15] Shakti and earth are spoken of as having chief worshipfulness; yet, because of non-existence and non-difference, that worshipfulness is not of man and Shiva souls.

[tal-a17-v16] In inert principles, for consciousness to abide, the teacher first performs the invocation-division and then acts from the fourth division.

[tal-a17-v17] From the union that ends in salutation, one should posit full being; then, from the union or excess of that form, full-nature-ness.

[tal-a17-v18] The excess of the object of meditation arises from the power of the meditator's humility; having invoked and worshipped, one satisfies; this is explained in Sri Svacchanda.

[tal-a17-v19] Our teachers said: not by this path alone; but that which is worshipful by transcendence is of independent consciousness nature.

[tal-a17-v20] Because his light is unlimited, nothing can be manifested anywhere; yet for him, worshipfulness, meditatableness, and the like shine forth.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-kuryāditi guruḥ prāha svarūpāpyāyanadvayāt / tāro varṇo@tha saṃbuddhipadaṃ tvāmityataḥ param uttamaikayutaṃ karmapadaṃ dīpakamapyataḥ / tabhyaṃ nāma caturthyantaṃ tato@pyucitadīpakam ityūhamantrayogena tattatkarma pravartayet / āvāhanānantaraṃ hi karma sarvaṃ nigadyate āvāhanaṃ ca saṃbodhaḥ svasvabhāvavyavasthiteḥ / bhāvasyāhaṃmayasvātmatādātmyāveśyamānatā śāktī bhūmiśca saivoktā yasyāṃ mukhyāsti pūjyatā / abhātatvādabhedācca nahyasau nṛśivātmanoḥ jaḍābhāseṣu tattveṣu saṃvitsthityai tato guruḥ / āvāhanavibhaktiṃ prāk kṛtvā turyavibhaktitaḥ namaskārāntatāyogātpūrṇāṃ sattāṃ prakalpayet / tataḥ pūrṇasvabhāvatvaṃ tadrūpodrekayogataḥ dhyeyodreko bhaveddhyātṛprahvībhāvavaśādyataḥ / āvāhyeṣṭvā pratarpyeti śrīsvacchande nirūpitam anenaiva pathāneyamityasmadguravo jaguḥ / paratvena tu yatpūjyaṃ tatsvatantracidātmakam anavacchitprakāśatvānna prakāśyaṃ tu kutracit / tasya hyetatprapūjyatvadhyeyatvādi yadullaset

chunks.l2:
[tal-a17-v21] How can enlightenment be in that form, when its independence causes difficult accomplishment?

[tal-a17-v22] In illumination, light would not be light without the power of object and the rest; the vocative ending alone is not enough.

[tal-a17-v23] To show what is taken from independence, there I perform this: 'I invoke the god'; then [I offer] a lamp to the god.

[tal-a17-v24] By prior utterance, the fullness-giving namaḥ, svāhā, and so forth may be praise; fullness increased by the conjunction of sun and moon is supreme.

[tal-a17-v25] One should ignite the nourishing, the sprinkling, and vauṣaṭ and the rest; there, even externally, action established in identity is urged.

[tal-a17-v26] If there is an action-word, the guru should sometimes infer it; it is employed for illuminating that unmanifested thing.

[tal-a17-v27] What is a mantra? It is that by which it becomes clear where it shines; by it, certainly, in sprinkling, pouring, japa, and similar rites.

[tal-a17-v28] Rather than accumulating that action, which makes one an obstructer, one should perform action-milking outside, where selfhood is absent.

[tal-a17-v29] Where a rite prescribes satisfaction, oblation, the enjoyer of oblations, burning of bonds, cutting, and similar acts, afterwards there are endless action-composed rites or acts.

[tal-a17-v30] What is to be accomplished by parts is not doubted there, as in initiation rites; then the disciple is tormented by a woman at the place of truth.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tasyaiva tatsvatantratvaṃ yātidurghaṭakāritā / saṃbodharūpe tattasmin kathaṃ saṃbodhanā bhavet prakāśanāyāṃ na syātprakāśasya prakāśatā / saṃbodhanavibhaktyaiva vinā karmādiśaktitām svātantryāttaṃ darśayituṃ tatrohamimamācaret / devamāvāhayāmīti tato devāya dīpakam prāgyuktyā pūrṇatādāyi namaḥsvāhādikaṃ bhavet / nutiḥ pūrṇatvamagnīndusaṃghaṭṭāpyāyatā param āpyāyakaṃ ca procchālaṃ vauṣaḍādi pradīpayet / tatra bāhye@pi tādātmyaprasiddhaṃ karma codyate yadi karmapadaṃ tanno gururabhyūhayetkvacit / anābhāsitatadvastubhāsanāya niyujyate mantraḥ kiṃ tena tatra syātsphuṭaṃ yatrāvabhāsi tat / tena prokṣaṇasaṃsekajapādividhiṣu dhruvam tatkarmābhyūhanaṃ kuryātpratyuta vyavadhātṛtām / bahistathātmatābhāve kāryaṃ karmapadohanam tṛptāvāhutihutabhukpāśaploṣacchidādiṣu / yatroddiṣṭe vidhau paścāttadanantaiḥ kriyātmakaiḥ aṃśaiḥ sādhyaṃ na tatroho dīkṣaṇādividhiṣviva / tataḥ śiṣyasya tattattvasthāne@streṇa pratāḍanam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a17-v31] Having done that, one should touch the heart with Shiva's hand; then, by one's own nadi path, one indeed reaches the child's heart.

[tal-a17-v32] Having gone to unity with the disciple-self, and having taken him folded in the heart, the one called swan-form, there by the dissolution seal.

[tal-a17-v33] He should make the illuminating one situated in his own heart [enter] the disciple's body by rays, separated only by rays.

[tal-a17-v34] Because one moves from the place of bondage, gains an independent place, and remains dependent on one's own action, one deserves birth everywhere.

[tal-a17-v35] Having first made the matter brought by that soul-heart, then in illusion he would create his bodies of that earth-principle.

[tal-a17-v36] There, for him, the conception rite is proper, together with the male-child rites and so on; one should perform a single sacrament up to birth from the womb.

[tal-a17-v37] Birth and the state of being enjoyer of enjoyments, united in one place, are purified; then, in those enjoyments, it makes his dissolution into that same identity.

[tal-a17-v38] Then one should practice severing those bonds of principles; and in this fourfold, impressions are further distinguished as higher and lower.

[tal-a17-v39] Of the mantras, the fifteen-fold [set] is supreme, or one should join in order eight beginning with pivanya and six weapons and the like; thus [it is] supreme.

[tal-a17-v40] These fifteen come about in order in the purification by dissolution; having first spoken the lower mantra, one proceeds from the mouth of the Self — and so the rite is joined.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-kṛtvātha śivahastena hṛdayaṃ parimarśayet / tataḥ svanāḍīmārgeṇa hṛdayaṃ prāpya vai śiśoḥ śiṣyātmanā sahaikatvaṃ gatvādāya ca taṃ hṛdā / puṭitaṃ haṃsarūpākhyaṃ tatra saṃhāramudrayā kuryādātmīyahṛdayasthitamapyavabhāsakam / śiṣyadehasya tejobhī raśmimātrāviyogataḥ svabandhasthānacalanāt svatantrasthānalābhataḥ / svakarmāparatantratvātsarvatrotpattimarhati tenātmahṛdayānītaṃ prākkṛtvā pudgalaṃ tataḥ / māyāyāṃ taddharātattvaśarīrāṇyasya saṃsṛjet tatrāsya garbhādhānaṃ ca yuktaṃ puṃsavanādibhiḥ / garbhaniṣkrāmaparyantairekāṃ kurvīta saṃskriyām jananaṃ bhogabhoktṛtvaṃ militvaikātha saṃskriyā / tato@sya teṣu bhogeṣu kuryāttanmayatāṃ layam tatastattattvapāśānāṃ vicchedaṃ samupācaret / saṃskārāṇāṃ catuṣke@sminnaparāṃ ca parāparām mantrāṇāṃ pañcadaśakaṃ parāṃ vā yojayetkramāt / pivanyādyaṣṭakaṃ śastrādikaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ parā tathā iti pañcadaśaite syuḥ kramāllīnatvasaṃskṛtau / aparāmantramuktvā prāgamukātmana ityatha

chunks.l2:
[tal-a17-v41] The teacher, saying 'I perform the impregnation rite,' should again utter that very mantra ending in svāhā and give three oblations.

[tal-a17-v42] Thus, of one born from the self of supreme-inferior mantra, I make supreme-inferior enjoyment-enjoyership.

[tal-a17-v43] Beforehand, having pronounced svāhā, let him offer three oblations; having uttered the drinking mantra of the self, thus then...

[tal-a17-v44] In enjoyment, I perform dissolution; then again the same mantra; and three oblations ending in svāhā should be given with ghee, sesame, and the like.

[tal-a17-v45] This indeed is the rule at the beginning of vomiting and at the end of fifteen: before, the mantra of the named self is supreme-self-related; thus then.

[tal-a17-v46] The supreme mantra is 'I do bond-cutting'; then, again from that, uttering hum, svaha, and phat together, one should give three offerings.

[tal-a17-v47] In this tetrad of saṃskāras, I have told the mantras; in them, before the karma term, one should speak the earth-principle term.

[tal-a17-v48] Then, having invoked and satisfied the lord of the earth principle, the guru, filled with devotion to Shiva, should instruct thus.

[tal-a17-v49] O lord of truth, by Shiva's command, you should not make an obstacle to this son's going to the disease-free place.

[tal-a17-v50] Then, if the mantrin wishes to purify separately the fivefold path beginning with the world, which enters the interval of the earth principle.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-garbhādhānaṃ karomīti punarmantraṃ tameva ca / svāhāntamuccarandadyādāhutitritayaṃ guruḥ paraṃ parāparāmantramamukātmana ityatha / jātasya bhogabhoktṛtvaṃ karomyatha parāparām ante svāheti proccārya vitarettisra āhutīḥ / uccārya pivanīmantramamukātmana ityatha bhoge layaṃ karomīti punarmantraṃ tameva ca / svāhāntamāhutīstisro dadyādājyatilādibhiḥ eṣa eva vamanyādau vidhiḥ pañcadaśāntake / pūrvaṃ parātmakaṃ mantramamukātmana ityatha pāśācchedaṃ karomīti parāmantraḥ punastataḥ / huṃ svāhā phaṭ samuccārya dadyāttisro@pyathāhutīḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ catuṣke@sminye mantrāḥ kathitā mayā / teṣu karmapadātpūrvaṃ dharātattvapadaṃ vadet tato dharātattvapatimāmantryeṣṭvā pratarpya ca / śivābhimānasaṃrabdho gururevaṃ samādiśet tattveśvara tvayā nāsya putrakasya śivājñayā / pratibandhaḥ prakartavyo yātuḥ padamanāmayam tato yadi samīheta dharātattvāntarālagam / pṛthak śodhayituṃ mantrī bhuvanādyadhvapañcakam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a17-v51] Without mantra, as before, one should offer three and three oblations and give the city, endowed with the reasoning 'I purify,' with a serene intellect.

[tal-a17-v52] Thus, in kalā, mantra, pada, and varṇa too, the expert should give three oblations each, separately or collectively.

[tal-a17-v53] Then, having given the full oblation with the supreme vauṣaṭ-ending, one should draw the disciple from another mantra, from one's own heart, and lead him.

[tal-a17-v54] When, however, through contemplation of inclusion in one pure principle, one should not separately purify beyond hearing the lord of truth.

[tal-a17-v55] Then, scattering the full [substance], one should lift the atom into the self and join it for the yoga of the self abiding in that state, with that other oblation.

[tal-a17-v56] Some think the guru would give it by an action-word, but other teachers say such a thing is made of contemplation.

[tal-a17-v57] Here an external offering should not be given separately to the teacher again; yet if one gives it, there is no fault, and that is a means in meditation.

[tal-a17-v58] Thus, when the former father's self is established, the guru should join; then the disciple's heart should be led; that self is of so many sounds.

[tal-a17-v59] Pure, for the attainment of firmness of that, and full by the supreme again; first the great Pashupata for purification of the reverse.

[tal-a17-v60] I offer again by weapon ending in vauṣaṭ; thus one should throw again the full [oblation]; then, having worshipped Maya, one should dismiss her.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-aparāmantrataḥ prāgvattisrastisrastadāhutīḥ / dadyātpuraṃ śodhayāmītyūhayuktaṃ prasannadhīḥ evaṃ kalāmantrapadavarṇeṣvapi vicakṣaṇaḥ / tisrastisro hutīrdadyāt pṛthak sāmastyato@pivā tataḥ pūrṇāhutiṃ dattvā parayā vauṣaḍantayā / aparāmantrataḥ śiṣyamuddhṛtyātmahṛdaṃ nayet yadā tvekena śuddhena tadantarbhāvacintanāt / na pṛthak śodhayettattvanāthasaṃśravaṇātparam tadā pūrṇāṃ vitīryāṇumutkṣipyātmani yojayet / tātsthyātmasaṃsthyayogāya tayaivāparayāhutīḥ sakarmapadayā dadyāditi kecittu manvate / anye tu guravaḥ prāhurbhāvanāmayamīdṛśam nātra bāhyāhutirdeyā daiśikasya pṛthak punaḥ / dadyādvā yadi no doṣaḥ syādupāyaḥ sa bhāvane evaṃ prāktanatātsthyātmasaṃsthatve yojayedguruḥ / tataḥ śiṣyahṛdaṃ neyaḥ sa ātmā tāvato@dhvanaḥ śuddhastaddārḍhyasiddhyai ca pūrṇā syātparayā punaḥ / mahāpāśupataṃ pūrvaṃ vilomasya viśuddhaye juhomi punarastreṇa vauṣaḍanta iti kṣipet / punaḥ pūrṇāṃ tato māyāmabhyarcyātha visarjayet

chunks.l2:
[tal-a17-v61] Meditate on the earth principle, purified and pure-formed, mixed with pure water fit for purification; then it becomes purified.

[tal-a17-v62] Thus, by increasingly mixing the preceding principles, the entire series of principles becomes Shiva; otherwise, if pure, they remain separate.

[tal-a17-v63] Separateness too is an impurity; it originates in what is called māyā; even when karma is exhausted, liberation would not be like that of the vidyeśvaras.

[tal-a17-v64] Then also, all invocation and the rest concerning the water element continue until the mixing of tejas in fire, in space, and in consciousness itself.

[tal-a17-v65] Thus, in due order, in the pure kala-principle, the kala should cut the bond resting on the arm; for that kala is of the nature of opening some agency.

[tal-a17-v66] He would burn up that knot, whose nature is the expansion of karma-named impurity, together with what goes to the spoon's tip, in the radiance of the fire-mantra, by a full oblation.

[tal-a17-v67] The mantra is all-form; by the power of refuge it becomes manifest form, and then in fire it burns bonds.

[tal-a17-v68] Burnt and with dissolved nature, the bond toward him, like Shambhu, attains only the remainder of the supreme lord's great radiance.

[tal-a17-v69] When the karma-bond is to be offered, all of his good and bad, inauspicious, present-past, and future—everything—is to be offered.

[tal-a17-v70] I burn; three phats; vauṣaṭ thus; the full offering should be thrown; thus, in the purification of māyā's end, the throat-noose also should be offered in fire.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-dharātattvaṃ viśuddhaṃ sajjalena śuddharūpiṇā / bhāvayenmiśritaṃ vāri śuddhiyogyaṃ tato bhavet tathā tattatpurātattvamiśraṇāduttarottaram / sarvā śivībhavettattvāvalī śuddhānyathā pṛthak pṛthaktvaṃ ca malo māyābhidhānastasya saṃbhave / karmakṣaye@pi no muktirbhavedvidyeśvarādivat tato@pi jalatattvasya vahnau vyomni cidātmake / āhvānādyakhilaṃ yāvattejasyasya vimaśraṇam evaṃ kramātkalātattve śuddhe pāśaṃ bhujāśritam / chindyātkalā hi sā kiṃcitkartṛtvonmīlanātmikā karmākhyamalajṛmbhātmā taṃ ca granthiṃ srugagragam / pūrṇāhutyā samaṃ vahnimantratejasi nirdahet mantro hi viśvarūpaḥ sannupāśrayavaśāttathā / vyaktarūpastato vahnau pāśaploṣavidhāyakaḥ pluṣṭo līnasvabhāvo@sau pāśastaṃ prati śambhuvat / parameśamahātejaḥśeṣamātratvamaśnute karmapāśe@tra hotavye pūrṇayāsya śubhāśubham / aśubhaṃ vā bhavadbhūtaṃ bhāvi vātha samastakam dahāmi phaṭtrayaṃ vauṣaḍiti pūrṇāṃ vinikṣipet / evaṃ māyāntasaṃśuddhau kaṇṭhapāśaṃ ca homayet

chunks.l2:
[tal-a17-v71] Of that full one, the maya-called, bond-breaking manifestation-natured [thing], I burn with three phaṭ; with vauṣaṭ the guru throws the full.

[tal-a17-v72] If it is to be made seedless, then here indeed one should cast another full mantra, endowed with the word of burning the seed called samaya-pāśa.

[tal-a17-v73] Devotion should be shown to the guru, to God, and to scripture; this is not a condition for the descent of power, for this is its very nature, not something separate.

[tal-a17-v74] At the end of māyā, when purity comes, the speech-lord who was formerly māyā full of power indeed attains the state of knowledge-power.

[tal-a17-v75] Having summoned pure knowledge, one should employ knowledge-power; thus, in order, when purified, the Sadashiva state too is sufficient.

[tal-a17-v76] Having cut the knotted crest, one should burn the impure boy, because in Sadashiva there are two bonds named authority and enjoyment.

[tal-a17-v77] Thus said, the anu bond is here; but the māyīya bond lasts until night. The student should bathe and sip as appropriate, and the teacher himself [is also implicated in this purification].

[tal-a17-v78] When the impurity called atomic is burnt up in the downward-flowing flame-impurity, then one contemplates all the knowables mentioned before.

[tal-a17-v79] Having joined the disciple's body with one's own body and life, one should make the universe from one's own body and life and remember it within.

[tal-a17-v80] By the stated procedure, one who is firm-minded and of undivided intellect has the place, time, and distance pair situated in prana, and prana is power-going.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-pūrṇasya tasya māyākhyaṃ pāśabhedaprathātmakam / dahāmi phaṭtrayaṃ vauṣaḍiti pūrṇāṃ kṣipedguruḥ nirbījā yadi kāryā tu tadātraivāparāṃ kṣipet / pūrṇāṃ samayapāśākhyabījadāhapadānvitām gurau deve tathā śāstre bhaktiḥ kāryāsya nahyasau / samayaḥ śaktipātasya svabhāvo hyeṣa no pṛthak māyānte śuddhimāyāte vāgīśī yā purābhavat / māyā śaktimayī saiva vidyāśaktitvamaśnute tacchuddhavidyāmāhūya vidyāśaktiṃ niyojayet / evaṃ krameṇa saṃśuddhe sadāśivapade@pyalam śikhāṃ granthiyutāṃ chittvā malamāṇavakaṃ dahet / yato@dhikārabhogākhyau dvau pāśau tu sadāśive ityuktyāṇavapāśo@tra māyīyastu niśāvadhiḥ / śiṣyo yathocitaṃ snāyādācāmeddaiśikaḥ svayam āṇavākhye vinirdagdhe hyadhovāhiśikhāmale / tataḥ prāguktasakalaprameyaṃ paricintayan śiṣyadehādimātmīyadehaprāṇādiyojitam / kṛtvātmadehaprāṇāderviśvamantaranusmaret uktaprakriyayā caivaṃ dṛḍhabuddhirananyadhīḥ / prāṇasthaṃ deśakālādhvayugaṃ prāṇaṃ ca śaktigam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a17-v81] That pure consciousness, gone into consciousness, is Shiva-formed; it is not different from the disciple's consciousness, nor from mantra, fire, and the rest.

[tal-a17-v82] Meditating, by the application as before, on Shiva who is with parts and partless, or two-natured, one may cast the full power by calmed faculties.

[tal-a17-v83] In the Traiśirasa Tantra it is said to be all-fulfilling; yet by the root-rising path it is flooded with the Shiva-moon.

[tal-a17-v84] But that knowledge-nectar which arises from the root stream in the cavity at the middle or end of birth and is agitated by the fierce rays of Shiva's sun.

[tal-a17-v85] By that, one should properly satisfy [him] with quieted senses; but [he is] radiant with rays of light in the middle of the lotus of the void-abode.

[tal-a17-v86] He is the grasp of the scripture of motionless knowledge of supported and support, and the striking impact of the one sphota of the world supported by birth.

[tal-a17-v87] Beginning from the root place and extending to the end of someśa, it stands like the sky; it is called thus only until tranquility.

[tal-a17-v88] It was said in the previous scripture: having filled the ladle with ghee and performed [the rite], the disciple, thus abiding in the self, remembers the root mantra.

[tal-a17-v89] Uniting Shiva, Shakti, oneself, the disciple, ghee, and fire, one slowly reaches the dvādaśānta with an undivided mind.

[tal-a17-v90] There, having adopted kumbhaka and meditating on the whole and the partless, one should stand undisturbed until the ghee is exhausted.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tāṃ ca saṃvidgatāṃ śuddhāṃ saṃvidaṃ śivarūpiṇīm / śiṣyasaṃvidabhinnāṃ ca mantravahnyādyabhedinīm dhyāyan prāgvatprayogeṇa śivaṃ sakalaniṣkalam / dvyātmakaṃ vā kṣipetpūrṇāṃ praśāntakaraṇena tu uktaṃ traiśirase tantre sarvasaṃpūraṇātmakam / mūlādudayagatyā tu śivenduparisaṃplutam janmāntamadhyakuharamūlasrotaḥsamutthitam / śivārkaraśmibhistīvraiḥ kṣubdhaṃ jñānāmṛtaṃ tu yat tena saṃtarpayetsamyak praśāntakaraṇena tu / śūnyadhāmābjamadhyasthaprabhākiraṇabhāsvaraḥ ādheyādhāraniḥspandabodhaśāstraparigrahaḥ / janmādheyaprapañcaikasphoṭasaṃghaṭṭaghaṭṭanaḥ mūlasthānātsamārabhya kṛtvā someśamantagam / khamivātiṣṭhate yāvatpraśāntaṃ tāvaducyate uktaṃ śrīpūrvaśāstre ca srucamāpūrya sarpiṣā / kṛtvā śiṣyaṃ tathātmasthaṃ mūlamantramanusmaran śivaṃ śaktiṃ tathātmānaṃ śiṣyaṃ sarpistathānalam / ekīkurvañchanairgaccheddvādaśāntamananyadhīḥ tatra kumbhakamāsthāya dhyāyansakalaniṣkalam / tiṣṭhettāvadanudvigno yāvadājyakṣayo bhvet

chunks.l2:
[tal-a17-v100] The speciality here is this: as long as life, the child's guru should, with full [power], create pure principle for the remaining function.

[tal-a17-v91] Thus, yoked in supreme reality by the guru who is of Shiva-form, one does not again attain beasthood, since the bondage of maya is burnt.

[tal-a17-v92] If, after the body falls, one again desires enjoyments in some principles, then through the differences of all and partial principles at the end one attains the supreme state.

[tal-a17-v93] Then, in that truth-ground, with undivided mind in that counting, one should again perform yoking between full offerings.

[tal-a17-v94] The initiation proclaimed as granting liberation, or granting both enjoyment and liberation, may be twofold: seeded or seedless.

[tal-a17-v95] Seedless initiation is to be performed for a child, for one whose death is unknown, for you when powerless, or by old age and the like, when the strength of power-descent arises.

[tal-a17-v96] In seedless samaya, one should purify the bonds too; one who has undergone seedless initiation is devoted to the deity, fire, and guru.

[tal-a17-v97] By this much indeed one may go to Shiva immediately, having enjoyed enjoyments, or, as stated in the Shri Dikshottara, in practice thirty-six angulas.

[tal-a17-v98] One should abandon, stage by stage, the worlds and truths that extend from foot to head; what remains is only an atom, partless, bodyless, that supreme self.

[tal-a17-v99] By power, there I cast him thus; but meditating, one should initiate. In a seeded initiation, however, one should not purify from time.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-evaṃ yuktaḥ pare tattve guruṇā śivamūrtinā / na bhūyaḥ paśutāmeti dagdhamāyānibandhanaḥ dehapāte punaḥ prepsedyadi tattveṣu kutracit / bhogān samastavyastatvabhedairante paraṃ padam tadā tattattvabhūmau tu tatsaṃkhyāyāmananyadhīḥ / punaryojanikāṃ kuryātpūrṇāhutyantareṇa tu muktipradā bhogamokṣapradā vā yā prakīrtitā / dīkṣā sā syātsabījatvanirbījātmatayā dvidhā bāle nirjñātamaraṇe tvaśakte vā jarādibhiḥ / kāryā nirbījikā dīkṣā śaktipātabalodaye nirbījāyāṃ sāmayāṃstu pāśānapi viśodhayet / kṛtanirbījadīkṣastu devāgnigurubhaktibhāk iyataiva śivaṃ yāyāt sadyo bhogān vibhujya vā / śrīmaddīkṣottare coktaṃ cāre ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgule tattvānyāpādamūrdhāntaṃ bhuvanāni tyajetkramāt / tuṭimātraṃ niṣkalaṃ tadadehaṃ tadahaṃparam śaktyā tatra kṣipāmyenamiti dhyāyaṃstu dīkṣayet / sabījāyāṃ tu dīkṣāyāṃ samayānna viśodhayet viśeṣastvayametasyāṃ yāvajjīvaṃ śiśorguruḥ / śeṣavṛttyai śuddhatattvasṛṣṭiṃ kurvīta pūrṇayā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a17-v101] One should meditate on the flowing light-form, casting the full net of tattvas, shining simultaneously from the ocean of Shiva-knowledge, which is not different.

[tal-a17-v102] One should create pure reality either by pot consecration, or by meditation power alone, or by complete consecrations.

[tal-a17-v103] Earth, his firm form, pervaded by Shiva-form, makes firm; that very earth, as meditation, becomes pure.

[tal-a17-v104] Water nourishes her, fire brings her radiance, and wind's joyful touch brings vastness to the sky.

[tal-a17-v105] Thus even the group of tanmatras is desired as made of Shiva-nature: supreme bliss, great pervasion, and release from all impurity.

[tal-a17-v106] To Shiva: going, taking, what is to be taken, and praise of Shiva; enough are Shiva's fragrance, abundance, taste, sight, and touch.

[tal-a17-v107] Thus, by hearing that, the senses become pure; possessing resolve and determination, light abides in attachment.

[tal-a17-v108] By the nature of Shiva-self, that which is to be done is purity in mind and the rest as a rule; coloring occurs together with agenthood by calculation.

[tal-a17-v109] Thus, for one who has ascended to Shiva-unity, this group of six coverings too is like sleep in the sphere of the portion of a rejectable thing.

[tal-a17-v110] Indeed the man who has attained Shiva-nature becomes pure; in principles such as vidyesha there is no impurity at all.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-abhinnācchivasaṃbodhajaladheryugapatsphurat / pūrṇāṃ kṣipaṃstattvajālaṃ dhyāyedbhārūpakaṃ sṛtam viśuddhatattvasṛṣṭiṃ vā kuryātkumbhābhiṣecanāt / tathā dhyānabalādeva yadvā pūrṇābhiṣecanaiḥ pṛthivī sthirarūpāsya śivarūpeṇa bhāvitā / sthirīkaroti tāmeva bhāvanāmiti śuddhyati jalamāpyāyayatyenāṃ tejo bhāsvaratāṃ nayet / marudānandasaṃsparśaṃ vyoma vaitatyamāvahet evaṃ tanmātravargo@pi śivatāmaya iṣyate / parānandamahāvyāptiraśeṣamalavicyutiḥ śive gantṛtvamādānamupādeyaśivastutiḥ / śivāmodabharāsvādadarśanasparśanānyalam tadākarṇanamityevamindriyāṇāṃ viśuddhatā / saṃkalpādhyavasāmānāḥ prakāśo raktisaṃsthitī śivātmatvena yatseyaṃ śuddhatā mānasādike / niyamo rañjanaṃ kartṛbhāvaḥ kalanayā saha vedanaṃ heyavastvaṃśaviṣaye suptakalpatā / itthaṃ śivaikyarūḍhasya ṣaṭkañcukagaṇo@pyayam śuddha eva pumān prāptaśivabhāvo viśuddhyati / vidyeśādiṣu tattveṣu naiva kācidaśuddhatā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a17-v111] Thus, through the creation of pure principles, even the disciple becomes made of them; this is indicated in the Śrīmālinīvijayottara.

[tal-a17-v112] The wise say that both bondage and liberation are the senses: restrained senses lead to bondage, while released senses lead to liberation.

[tal-a17-v113] These, when in the pervasive state together with mind, may be released; but those, somewhere in an object, from obstruction, lead to bondage.

[tal-a17-v114] Thus, in the Siddhayogishvara view, the state of the senses is declared to be twofold, distinguished as pure and impure.

[tal-a17-v115] The glorious knowledge-teacher says to you: in the seeing of authority and praise, in initiation with all mantras, this rule is said.

[tal-a17-v116] In purification ending in māyā, all actions would always be by the lower twofold-natured; but at the end of the manifest, in the unmanifest, by the supreme alone.

[tal-a17-v117] Considering this rule—five limbs from pivana and the rest to īśa, ending with the whole—the supreme teacher should perform the action.

[tal-a17-v118] On the former path, the countable number of offerings of truth and color should be doubled on the word path, becoming fourfold.

[tal-a17-v119] Along the mantra-kalā path, by gradual steps the measure doubles and doubles until the three principles are purified, then it becomes twentyfold.

[tal-a17-v120] For each rite, in the three-principle there would be sixty oblations; in the one-principle they say one hundred and eight oblations.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ityevaṃ śuddhatattvānāṃ sṛṣṭyā śiṣyo@pi tanmayaḥ / bhaveddhyetatsūcitaṃ śrīmālinīvijayottare bandhamokṣāvubhāvetāvindriyāṇi jagurbudhāḥ / nigṛhītāni bandhāya vimuktāni vimuktaye etāni vyāpake bhāve yadā syurmanasā saha / muktāni kvāpi viṣaye rodhādbandhāya tāni tu ityevaṃ dvividho bhāvaḥ śuddhāśuddhaprabhedataḥ / indriyāṇāṃ samākhyātaḥ siddhayogīśvare mate śrīmān vidyāgurustvāha pramāṇastutidarśane / samastamantrairdīkṣāyāṃ niyamastveṣa kathyate māyāntaśuddhau sarvāḥ syuḥ kriyā hyaparayā sadā / dvyātmayā sakalānte tu niṣkale parayaiva tu īśānte ca pivanyādi sakalānte@ṅgapañcakam / ityevaṃvidhimālocya karma kuryādgurūttamaḥ purādhvani hutīnāṃ yā saṃkhyeyaṃ tattvavarṇayoḥ / tāmeva dviguṇīkuryātpadādhvani caturguṇām kramānmantrakalāmārge dviguṇā dviguṇā kramāt / yāvattritattvasaṃśuddhau syādviṃśatiguṇā tataḥ pratikarma bhavetṣaṣṭirāhutīnāṃ tritattvake / ekatattve śataṃ prāhurāhutīnāṃ tu sāṣṭakam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a17-v121] The full oblations declared together with the reverse rite have no difference in number in the purification of all paths.

[tal-a17-v122] Thus this initiation, endowed with birth and the rest, has been explained.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-vilomakarmaṇā sākaṃ yāḥ pūrṇāhutayaḥ smṛtāḥ / tāsāṃ sarvādhvasaṃśuddhau saṃkhyānyatvaṃ na kiṃcana ityeṣā kathitā dīkṣā jananādisamanvitā
